en-US.name: grate
en-US.releaseNotes:
grate 2.2.0 brings migration correctness fixes, improved Oracle and SQL Server script parsing, .NET 11 RC3 support, and stronger verification of the packages you install.

## Highlights

• Add .NET 11 RC3 support while retaining .NET 8, 9 and 10 assets in the NuGet libraries and .NET tool. Self-contained binaries and the Docker image bundle runtime `11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148`. See the [packaging guide](https://grate-devs.github.io/grate/packaging/) for runtime and distribution details. (#868)
• Bundle the `use-grate` coding-agent skill, including guidance and runnable SQLite examples. Install it explicitly with `grate skills install --local` or `grate skills install --global`. (#822)
• Forward additional Docker container arguments to grate, alongside the environment-based configuration. (#827)
• Update to System.CommandLine 2.0.14, parse arguments once, and handle help and validation errors before creating database services. (#845)

## Fixes

• Improve Oracle statement splitting for SQL terminators, PL/SQL packages, anonymous blocks, local routines and CASE expressions. (#816, #858, #859, #866)
• Preserve bracketed and double-quoted SQL Server identifiers containing `GO`, including escaped delimiters, and split only on standalone batch-separator lines. (#864)
• Prevent dry runs from creating, dropping or restoring databases and from writing migration history. SQLite previews use read-only connections for existing files. (#852)
• Isolate connections, cached history, deferred writes and results between differently configured migrators, so `WithConfiguration()` targets the requested database. (#861)
• Stop migrations when version registration or final status updates fail, instead of silently attributing scripts to an older version. Retain compatibility with legacy tracking-table upgrades. (#862)
• Preserve the version record when changed one-time scripts are accepted with `--warnandignoreononetimescriptchanges`, keeping history references valid without executing the changed SQL. (#863)
• Derive administration connection strings without changing credentials or the meaning of quoted values, key ordering and provider aliases. (#865)
• Fix SQL Server permissions-script hangs during transactional migrations. Refresh history between attempts and update the cache only after a successful history write or enqueue, allowing retries after rollback. (#828, #876)
• Wait for a working target connection after custom database-creation scripts and propagate the final connection failure if readiness cannot be established. (#877)
• Recognize legacy RoundhousE script hashes across line-ending changes, preserving the existing normalized hash format for new history. Expand the [RoundhousE migration guidance](https://grate-devs.github.io/grate/migrating-from-roundhouse/). (#842)
• Fix MariaDB bootstrap on servers with case-insensitive database names (`lower_case_table_names=1`), including upgrades and recovery from interrupted internal bootstrap. (#893)
• Update runtime, native SQLite and database-driver dependencies, and improve package verification and Windows Arm64 MSI generation. (#817, #839, #868)

## Distribution, testing and documentation

• Automate release packaging and publication, with checksums and a release manifest for the nine CLI ZIPs, two Windows MSIs and two Debian packages. The release workflow also builds the .NET tool, six libraries and a verified multi-architecture Docker image. (#804)
• Use `gratedevs/grate` as the canonical Docker image, with matching image digests published to `erikbra/grate` during the compatibility transition. (#804)
• Add native MSI installation, upgrade and uninstall checks on Windows x64/Arm64; Debian installation, package upgrade and purge checks on Linux amd64/Arm64; and default Docker entrypoint checks on Alpine amd64/Arm64. These exercise migrations and reruns as well as package lifecycle behavior. (#883)
• Expand Windows and cross-framework test coverage, packaged-library/tool checks, migration reporting and recovery regressions, and native MSI security analysis. (#820, #843, #868, #804)
• Document application versus internal migration tables, changed-script handling and hash history, and the maintainer release process. Prepare source-built Homebrew/core packaging while retaining the existing cask channel. (#840, #879, #804, #805)

## Upgrade notes

### Custom database providers：statement-splitting API

`ISyntax.StatementSeparatorRegex` has been replaced by `IStatementSplitter StatementSplitter`. Custom implementations of `ISyntax` must now supply an `IStatementSplitter`; consumers of the removed `StatementSeparatorRegex` property must migrate to the splitter API. The corresponding property on `AnsiSqlDatabase` has also been removed. Rebuild and update custom providers when upgrading the libraries.

Normal CLI use and applications using the bundled providers require no changes for this API update.

### Transaction isolation

New migration transactions started by `--transaction` use `ReadCommitted` isolation to avoid SQL Server history-locking hangs. When joining a caller-owned transaction, grate retains that transaction's existing isolation level. A caller-selected `Serializable` transaction can still encounter the original locking behavior.

### Docker entrypoint

The default entrypoint continues to read environment-based configuration and now forwards additional container arguments to grate. Supply `APP_CONNSTRING` when using it; SQL scripts and migration output use `/db` and `/output`. For a help-only invocation without database configuration, use:

```sh
docker run --rm --entrypoint /app/grate gratedevs/grate:2.2.0 --help
```

### Windows installers and package managers

The x64 and Arm64 MSIs use corrected per-user installer identities. If you installed a `2.2.0` prerelease MSI, uninstall it before installing the final `2.2.0`：packages with the same numeric version and different prerelease identities require explicit uninstall/reinstall.

The release workflow prepares a WinGet candidate under `grate-devs.grate`; submission and public acceptance are separate steps. Follow the [WinGet migration guide](https://github.com/grate-devs/grate/blob/2.2.0/installers/winget/MIGRATION.md) for transitions from `erikbra.grate`.

The existing Homebrew cask remains `erikbra/cask/grate`. The proposed Homebrew/core formula is separate work; `brew install grate` is not yet an available installation route. See the [packaging guide](https://grate-devs.github.io/grate/packaging/) for channel details.
